doc.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021

title: 92nd Infantry Band, Fort Huachuca to Europe
summary: Allen joins the forming 28-piece 92nd Division band at Fort Huachuca, then moves through Texas and Mississippi and ships to Europe in a 1945 convoy.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well I’ve got an awful lot I’d like to talk about it in about an hour, but I’m interested in when you were a young man and you joined the military, the now famous 92nd Infantry — the Buffalo soldiers.

Yeah that was my first assignment there, they was forming a 28-piece military band that they needed at Fort Huachuca at 92nd Division, Buffalo Division. And they needed a band. So I was in Fort Meade so I went to sign up for assignment to go, what I wanted to do, so I wanted to play music. So they said oh yeah we have a vacancy of 28 people, we’ve got to get 28 people to make up this Army band, the 92nd, the 370th Infantry Band.

They sent me to Fort Huachuca, me and about five people went to Fort Huachuca to join the band. They was making the band. They only had about five people there and they needed 28 pieces, to replace a military band you know.
And then you found yourself in Paris eventually?

Well yeah, but first I went to the 92nd Division, so when they had to go to the mountains in Italy they transferred the band to headquarters in Sam Houston, Texas, and they put, attached us to the 2nd Calvary Division in Fort Clark, Texas. And from there we went to
Mississippi and we stayed out there and then from Mississippi we went to Europe in a convoy, a 13-ship convoy. They went in 1945.
